newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares end lower, seen opening stable.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares end lower, seen opening stable.

text.p: Chilean shares closed lower with turnover boosted by $47.5 million stock offering by department store chain Almacenes Paris, said dealers.
The bolsa is seen holding steady at the opening with the market sensitive to news especially in the electricity scetor which has been volatile in recent weeks, they said.
The 40-share IPSA index ended down 0.18 percent at 95.65 points. The general IGPA index shed 0.18 percent to 5,219.12 points.
Turnover was a strong 30.6 billion pesos with the Almacenes Paris share issue accounting for two thirds of the volume.
Thursday's offer was the last stage of a $80 million issue, which started to be sold to private investors last week.

Traders reported the market was hurt by profit-taking after Wednesday's rally, which was driven by the success of a group led by power utility Enersis in buying Brazilian electricity distributor Cerj.
The Cerj acquisition is unlikely to have a major impact on Enersis' profits, which are under pressure from lower generating and distribution tariffs in Chile, said Salomon Brothers.
"This is a relatively small privatization for Chilectra and Enersis with minute per-share earnings impact potential," said the report.
Enersis ended up 0.41 percent at 247 pesos.
Losers included forestry stocks on fresh fears of a drop wood pulp prices, said traders.
Forestry firm Inforsa ended down 4.11 percent at 70 pesos with board-maker Masisa dropping 2.53 pesos to 193 pesos.
